class.name: GameplayTagsManager
class.brief_description: Singleton that merges every [GameplayTagTable] into one lookup and owns the canonical tag instances.
class.description: Built by [World] before the game instance is created, so tag tables are always loaded before anything can reference a tag. Tables are merged in the order they are listed in the project setting and the first declaration of a name wins; a duplicate declaration warns and is ignored. Every registered tag has a source, reported by [method get_tag_source_kind]: [code]TAG_SOURCE_TABLE[/code] for a declared tag, [code]TAG_SOURCE_IMPLICIT[/code] for a parent implied by a longer one, and [code]TAG_SOURCE_RUNTIME[/code] for a name nothing declared. That last case is the one to watch. [method request_tag] never fails on a well-formed name - it registers the tag and warns rather than returning null - so a typo, or a name left behind by a deleted table entry, becomes a real and usable tag. Absence of an error does not mean the tag was spelled correctly.

method.name: destroy_singleton
method.description: Tears the manager down. The extension calls this on unload; a project has no reason to.

method.name: get_all_tag_names
method.description: Every registered name, from every source.

method.name: get_loaded_table_paths
method.description: The tables currently merged, in the order they were listed in [code]application/game_framework/gameplay_tag_tables[/code].

method.name: get_separated_tag
method.description: Splits [param tag] into the chain of tags leading to it: [code]A.B.C[/code] yields [code]A[/code], [code]A.B[/code], [code]A.B.C[/code].

method.name: get_singleton
method.description: The manager, created on first use. It is not an autoload and does not appear in the scene tree.

method.name: get_tag
method.description: The canonical tag for [param tag_name], or null if nothing registered it. Use this when a miss should stay a miss.

method.name: get_tag_description
method.description: The description [param tag_name] was declared with, or an empty string.

method.name: get_tag_source_kind
method.description: Where [param tag_name] came from. [constant TAG_SOURCE_RUNTIME] is how you find typos.

method.name: get_tag_source_path
method.description: The [GameplayTagTable] that declares [param tag_name], or an empty string for an implicit or runtime tag, which no single table owns.

method.name: has_tag
method.description: Whether [param tag_name] is known - declared by a table, implied as an ancestor, or conjured at runtime.

method.name: initialize_tags
method.description: Rebuilds the whole lookup from the project setting. Safe to call again at any time: tag instances that survive the rebuild are reused, so references already handed out keep pointing at the canonical tag. [World] calls this before it creates the [GameInstance], so tags are resolvable from [method GameInstance._on_init] onward.

method.name: is_valid_tag_name
method.description: The rule the table loader applies, exposed so the editor can reject a bad name at authoring time instead of silently dropping it on the next load.

method.name: request_tag
method.description: The canonical tag for [param tag_name], [b]registering it if nothing declared it[/b]. It never returns null for a well-formed name: an asset that outlived its table still yields a usable tag instead of a null, at the cost of turning a typo into a real tag. Such tags report [constant TAG_SOURCE_RUNTIME] and the editor pickers show them in red.

constants.constant: Declared in a [GameplayTagTable]; [method get_tag_source_path] names the table.
An ancestor implied by a longer declared tag - [code]A.B[/code] registered because some table declares [code]A.B.C[/code]. Owned by no single table, since several may imply the same ancestor.
Conjured on demand by [method request_tag] because nothing declared it - usually a typo, or a name left behind by a deleted table entry.
